page: Amazon Web Services r8gn.12xlarge is an arm64 memory-optimized virtual machine built on the AWS Nitro System. Powered by AWS Graviton4 processors utilizing the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 microarchitecture, the instance provides 48 dedicated physical cores running at 2.8 GHz without simultaneous multithreading. It is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside a 36 MB L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and 64 KB of L1 data cache. The instance features a baseline network bandwidth of 150 Gbps and does not include bundled local storage or hardware GPUs, necessitating remote Amazon EBS volumes for persistent storage.

Benchmark evaluations reveal top-tier memory and multi-threaded processing throughput. Memory bandwidth tests demonstrate 429.61 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads and 209.89 GB/sec on uncached writes, placing the instance in the top 10 percent of its class. The dedicated 48-core configuration yields high multi-core scaling, reaching a Geekbench multi-core score of 23591.0, Clang compilation throughput of 68445.0, and stress-ng multi-core capacity of 81819.24. In contrast, single-core metrics remain moderate, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1862.0 and stress-ng single-core score of 1706.28, reflecting predictable execution rather than peak single-threaded frequency.

The 150 Gbps network profile and memory architecture deliver exceptional data ingestion and transport rates, evidenced by 94.95 GB/sec in static web throughput, 47475.08 in PassMark database operations, and 99.9 million Redis SET operations per second. Hardware cost efficiency is driven by the density of physical ARMv9 cores and high-throughput memory channels, which reduce overhead compared to traditional hyperthreaded x86 architectures. However, workloads requiring dense local NVMe storage or heavy single-thread burst performance must account for reliance on networked storage and moderate single-core speeds.

Amazon Web Services r8gn.12xlarge is best suited for large-scale in-memory caches, distributed databases, large memory-resident analytics, continuous integration build clusters, and high-throughput network proxy layers that can saturate wide network pipelines and parallel memory structures.
description: Amazon Web Services r8gn.12xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server driven by the AWS Graviton4 ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture. It features 48 dedicated physical vCPUs clocked at 2.8 GHz, 384.0 GB of RAM (an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio), and a 150 Gbps baseline network pipeline, operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor without local disk storage or GPU accelerators. The instance delivers top-tier memory bandwidth, achieving 429.61 GB/sec on large read blocks and 209.89 GB/sec on writes, alongside strong parallel processing seen in its Geekbench multi-core score of 23591.0 and 99.9 million Redis SET operations per second. While single-thread benchmarks are standard, the absence of SMT guarantees dedicated execution capacity across all cores. These characteristics make r8gn.12xlarge efficient for high-concurrency databases, Redis clusters, memory-intensive data analytics, and large CI/CD compilation workloads.
